entries.title: Claude Fable 5 — new Mythos-class model
entries.paragraph: Claude Code 2.1.170 adds access to Claude Fable 5, a Mythos-class model Anthropic describes as exceeding any model they had previously made generally available. Update to 2.1.170+ to select it.
entries.whyItMatters: A new top-tier model is now selectable for your hardest agentic tasks — worth benchmarking against Opus on your real workloads before committing.

entries.title: Sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents (up to 5 levels deep)
entries.paragraph: Sub-agents may now dispatch their own sub-agents, nesting up to 5 levels. The same release fixes WebFetch(domain:*.example.com) wildcard rules never matching subdomains, and stuck 1M-context sessions now auto-compact back under the standard limit instead of hanging.
entries.whyItMatters: Deeper agent trees let an orchestrator decompose work recursively instead of flattening everything into one fan-out — but each level multiplies token spend, so cap depth deliberately.

entries.title: New --safe-mode, /cd, and disableBundledSkills
entries.paragraph: --safe-mode (and CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE) starts Claude Code with every customization — CLAUDE.md, plugins, skills, hooks, MCP servers — disabled for troubleshooting. /cd moves a session to a new working directory without breaking the prompt cache. A disableBundledSkills setting hides built-in skills, workflows, and slash commands from the model, and self-hosted runners gain a post-session lifecycle hook.
entries.whyItMatters: --safe-mode is the fastest way to prove whether your own config is causing a bug, and disableBundledSkills trims the model's tool surface in locked-down setups.

example.code: claude --safe-mode   # start with CLAUDE.md, plugins, skills, hooks, MCP all off

entries.title: availableModels allowlist is now strictly enforced
entries.paragraph: Two releases tighten model allowlisting. 2.1.175 adds the enforceAvailableModels managed setting: when on, the allowlist also constrains the Default model, and user or project settings can no longer widen a managed list. 2.1.176 stops alias picks from being redirected to a blocked model via ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL, and /fast now refuses to toggle if it would switch to a model outside the allowlist. The same release also generates session titles in your conversation's language and adds a footerLinksRegexes setting for regex-matched footer link badges.
entries.whyItMatters: If your org pins models via availableModels, the env-var and /fast escape hatches are now closed — verify your allowlist still includes every model your team actually needs.

entries.title: claude-fable-5 model and fable alias added to SDK types
entries.paragraph: The SDK model types now include claude-fable-5 and the fable alias, reaching parity with Claude Code 2.1.170 so you can target Fable 5 from typed SDK code without casting around the type system.
entries.whyItMatters: TypeScript consumers can select the new model with full type safety the day it ships.

entries.title: system/model_fallback now fires for all fallback triggers
entries.paragraph: SDK consumers now receive the system/model_fallback message for every fallback trigger — overloaded, server_error, and last_resort in addition to the existing model_not_found and permission_denied. The message's trigger field gained the two new values.
entries.whyItMatters: You can now observe and react to every reason a model was swapped under you — useful for logging degraded runs or surfacing them to users.

entries.title: Fixed dropped turn results and lost agent state on SDK resume
entries.paragraph: Two resume and concurrency fixes: turn result messages were being dropped when multiple turns completed while a background agent or workflow was running, and background-agent, remote-agent, and MCP task state was not restored when resuming a session via the SDK.
entries.whyItMatters: If you build long-running or resumable agents on the SDK, completions and in-flight task state now survive resume instead of being silently lost.

entries.title: Per-plugin skipMcpDiscovery option
entries.paragraph: The SDK plugins option now accepts skipMcpDiscovery: true per plugin, so a host that manages a plugin's MCP connections itself can load that plugin's skills and hooks without the engine re-reading its .mcp.json. Also fixed slash-then-whitespace input (e.g. / add tests) being silently dropped instead of treated as a plain prompt.
entries.whyItMatters: Hosts that own their MCP wiring can adopt plugins for skills and hooks without double-connecting MCP servers.

entries.title: Web search in code mode · richer MCP tool schemas (oneOf/allOf)
entries.paragraph: Code mode can now call standalone web search directly, including from nested JavaScript tool calls, returning plaintext results. Tool and connector input schemas now preserve oneOf and allOf, and large schemas keep more shallow structure when compacted — improving compatibility with richer MCP tools. codex doctor also reports editor and pager environment details (redacted in JSON output).
entries.whyItMatters: If you expose MCP tools with union or intersection input schemas to Codex, they now round-trip correctly instead of being flattened away.

entries.title: /app handoff to Codex Desktop · image file paths exposed to the model
entries.paragraph: The /app command hands the current CLI thread into Codex Desktop on macOS and native Windows. Local image attachments and generated images now expose their saved file paths to the model, making follow-up edits and file references more reliable. App-server integrations can read account token usage, and auth now supports v2 personal access tokens.
entries.whyItMatters: Exposing image file paths means multi-step image edits land on the intended file instead of the model guessing from conversation history.

suggestions.title: Audit your model allowlist before upgrading
suggestions.paragraph: If your team pins models with a managed availableModels list, the env-var and /fast escape hatches are now closed. Before rolling out 2.1.175+, confirm the allowlist contains every model your developers actually use, including whatever the Default resolves to.
suggestions.whyItMatters: A too-narrow allowlist will now hard-block developers instead of silently falling back to an allowed model.

suggestions.title: Cap nesting depth and token budget in recursive agent trees
suggestions.paragraph: With sub-agents now able to spawn sub-agents up to 5 deep, a recursive orchestrator can blow past your token budget fast. If your service drives Claude Code agents, set an explicit budget and prefer pipelining over deep nesting unless a task genuinely needs it.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Each nesting level multiplies fan-out; an unbounded tree is the easiest way to 10x a run's cost.

suggestions.title: Log every model fallback in SDK-based agents
suggestions.paragraph: If your Node or TypeScript service embeds the Agent SDK, subscribe to system/model_fallback and record the trigger (now including overloaded, server_error, and last_resort). Surface degraded runs in your own metrics rather than letting silent model swaps skew your results.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Knowing when and why you were downgraded is the difference between a debuggable incident and a mystery quality dip.
suggestions.tiesTo: Claude Agent SDK · v0.3.174 · Jun 12 — model_fallback message

suggestions.title: Reach for --safe-mode first when a session misbehaves
suggestions.paragraph: When Claude Code behaves oddly, restart with --safe-mode to disable all customizations (CLAUDE.md, plugins, skills, hooks, MCP). If the problem disappears, the cause is your config — re-enable pieces until it returns.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Bisecting config with a single flag is far faster than guessing which hook or MCP server broke.

suggestions.title: Keep MCP tool input schemas expressive but shallow
suggestions.paragraph: Codex 0.139 now preserves oneOf/allOf in tool and connector schemas. If you author MCP servers, you can use union and intersection types for tool inputs and expect richer clients to honor them — but keep the schemas shallow so schema compaction on large tool sets stays lossless.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Expressive-but-shallow schemas give the model a precise input contract without being truncated when a client compacts many tools.
suggestions.tiesTo: Codex · v0.139.0 · Jun 9 — oneOf/allOf in tool schemas
